title: Why Every Child Carried a Gas Mask Box
hook: You couldn't board a school bus without your cardboard box.

scenes.text: At the outbreak of World War II, the British government issued thirty-eight million gas masks to every man, woman, and baby.
scenes.imagePrompt: 1940s schoolroom wooden cloakroom with rows of cardboard gas mask boxes hanging from brass coat pegs. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: At the outbreak of World War II, the British government issued thirty-eight million gas masks to every man, woman, and baby.

scenes.text: Every child was required by law to carry their square cardboard box on a canvas string everywhere: to school, parks, and cinemas.
scenes.imagePrompt: Vintage wooden school desk with open notebook, dip inkwell pen, and square brown cardboard box resting on the corner. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Every child was required by law to carry their square cardboard box on a canvas string everywhere: to school, parks, and cinemas.

scenes.text: Bus conductors refused boarding to anyone who forgot their box, and headmasters conducted surprise gas drills during arithmetic class.
scenes.imagePrompt: Interior of a 1940s red London double-decker bus with wooden floorboards and leather seats by the window. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Bus conductors refused boarding to anyone who forgot their box, and headmasters conducted surprise gas drills during arithmetic class.

scenes.text: For toddlers, masks were terrifying rubber contraptions. To comfort them, the government produced red and blue 'Mickey Mouse' respirators.
scenes.imagePrompt: Nursery wooden shelf with a vintage rubber child's respirator featuring bright red rubber fittings and eye glass lenses. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: For toddlers, masks were terrifying rubber contraptions. To comfort them, the government produced red and blue 'Mickey Mouse' respirators.

scenes.text: Babies were placed into sealed airtight steel pods with manual hand bellows that mothers had to pump continuously.
scenes.imagePrompt: Vintage metal baby carrier apparatus with clear glass observation window and rubber accordion hand pump. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Babies were placed into sealed airtight steel pods with manual hand bellows that mothers had to pump continuously.

scenes.text: Fortunately, poison gas was never used on British cities. Would you have remembered your gas mask box every single morning?
